title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook and quality gating metrics
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds CI hook to run prompt-set regression checks and fail on quality gating threshold regressions; non-breaking; enables teams to catch prompt regressions before merge.
description: Motivation: Several recent incidents were traced back to prompt-set regressions introduced by model/serving changes. This PR adds a lightweight CI hook that runs the eval-harness prompt regression suite on each PR and enforces quality gates based on configurable eval metrics. Goals: 1) surface regressions against canonical prompt sets early; 2) make gating configurable per-repo and per-branch; 3) provide clear actionable diffs in CI for failed prompts. Changes: - New GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/eval-prompt-regression.yml that runs a targeted eval-harness job for changed prompts and for smoke coverage when model config changes. - Eval harness CLI extension (eval_harness/ci_hook.py) which accepts --changed-files and --gate-config and emits a compact JSON summary for CI. - Gate configuration file eval_harness/gates/default_gates.yaml with defaults (exact_match_threshold, rouge_l, semantic_score) and per-prompt overrides. - Integration with diagnostic output under artifacts/ which includes failing prompt examples, metric deltas, and recommended revert notes. - Unit tests and e2e tests under tests/eval_harness to validate gating logic and action behavior. Checklist: - [x] Add GH Action workflow and permissions - [x] Implement CI CLI hook - [x] Add default gate config and documentation - [x] Add tests and CI flakiness guard - [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md with how to interpret gating failures How it works in CI: When a PR is opened or updated the workflow identifies changed prompt files and model config changes. The CI job runs the eval-harness on the intersection of changed prompts (or a small smoke set on model changes), computes metrics, compares them to the gate thresholds in default_gates.yaml and repo overrides, and fails the job if any metric regression exceeds the configured delta. The job uploads artifact JSON with a per-prompt breakdown and a human-readable summary file that links to the failing examples. Backwards compatibility and opt-out: The gating is opt-out via repo-level .github/eval_gates.yaml. Existing repos will inherit default_gates.yaml. Performance: The workflow is parallelized across prompt shards and will short-circuit on clear large regressions to save CI minutes. Considerations: - Gate thresholds are intentionally conservative and team-configurable. - Model-owner teams should add larger prompt sets to their repo to get stronger coverage. Related: ENG-2034 adds a dashboard to track CI-failing prompts over time. This PR is intentionally single-purpose and does not change runtime serving code. Documentation: Added docs in docs/eval-ci.md with examples and instructions for adding per-repo gates. QA notes: e2e runs were executed against the 'canary' model profile; small transient flakiness observed on semantic scoring in 2/40 runs; test adjusted with a retry in the CI wrapper. Merge: squash and merge after approvals and CI green.
